author: Times News
description:
Iran’s control over the Strait of Hormuz does not appear to be easing. Since the start of the war, European natural gas prices have increased by 60 per cent. If President Trump does not find a way to alleviate the threat on the waterway, countries around the world will continue to see oil and gas prices surge.

Trump has some options to restore the flow of ships through the Strait, but how effective or escalatory these might be is unknown. European nations, along with Japan, have signalled their readiness to help secure shipping through the Strait. Trump has also threatened to hold Kharg Island, Iran’s crown jewel in terms of crude oil export, ransom. If all else fails, Iran’s threat on the Strait may force Trump’s hand in a full-scale ground invasion; something we have not seen since the 2003 invasion of Iraq.
